grh_539867e84857877551fd.title: Mission Accomplished
paragraphs: Ten-year-old Joni Love has taken seriously the last assignment her father gave her before he was killed during the war: look after her mother and make sure she is happy. Deciding that her lonely mother needs another husband, Joni first asks bachelor Dr. Christian to marry her. He gently declines but agrees to help. The better prospect turns out to be returning Major Miller, owner of the local radio station that Leslie Love has competently managed during his military service. Because their correspondence was signed simply 'Leslie Love,' Miller had assumed his wartime station manager was a man and initially has difficulty accepting that a woman has run the operation so well. Meeting Leslie quickly changes his attitude. Joni notices that her mother likes the younger major and that he likes both mother and daughter, and cheerfully shifts her matchmaking plan from Dr. Christian to Miller, satisfied that she is finally carrying out her father's mission to keep her mother from being alone.

grh_532fc4a9fc58d1889520.title: Sterling Silver
paragraphs: As Rivers End's old opera house is about to be demolished, Dr. Christian remembers Sterling Silver, the melodrama actor who was his boyhood hero. The past suddenly becomes a real mystery when owner Sam Roberts is shot, valuable antique playbills disappear and one of Silver's ornate pistols is found at the scene. Sam believes the now-elderly actor attacked him over a thirty-thousand-dollar promissory note, but Dr. Christian cannot reconcile that accusation with the man he remembers. Returning to the dark theater with police, he traps the real thief, who had clubbed Silver, stolen one of his pistols, accidentally shot Sam and hidden both Silver and the stolen playbills among the stage props. Silver survives, the old debt is explained as an investment gone bad rather than a betrayal, and Dr. Christian gets one final chance to remember the theater as it was before demolition.
